es: Distinguir en una noticia los hechos verificables, las afirmaciones sin prueba y las opiniones, y reconocer sus señales.

vocabulary.es: rumores, lo que se oye decir
al pie de la letra, sin cuestionarlo

teaching.en: Anything presented as a verifiable fact should pass a simple test: can an independent reader verify it in a public record?
teaching.es: Todo lo que se presenta como un hecho comprobable debería superar una prueba sencilla: ¿puede un lector independiente verificarlo en un registro público?
teaching.explanationEs: Verify es el verbo de la comprobación; un hecho se apoya en un registro, no en quien lo cuenta.
segments: Anything presented as a verifiable fact should pass a simple test:
can an independent reader verify it in a public record?
teaching.audioText: Anything presented as a verifiable fact should pass a simple test: can an independent reader verify it in a public record?

teaching.en: The report says the minister allegedly accepted gifts, which remains an unsupported claim until someone produces hard evidence.
teaching.es: El informe dice que el ministro supuestamente aceptó regalos, lo que sigue siendo una afirmación sin respaldo hasta que alguien presente pruebas sólidas.
teaching.explanationEs: Allegedly avisa de que nadie ha demostrado lo que sigue; hard evidence es incontable.
segments: The report says the minister allegedly accepted gifts, which
remains an unsupported claim until someone produces hard evidence.
teaching.audioText: The report says the minister allegedly accepted gifts, which remains an unsupported claim until someone produces hard evidence.

teaching.en: A witness who repeats what a neighbour said is offering hearsay, and an anonymous source who cannot be named deserves extra caution.
teaching.es: Un testigo que repite lo que dijo un vecino ofrece rumores, y una fuente anónima que no puede nombrarse merece aún más cautela.
teaching.explanationEs: Hearsay es incontable: no lleva artículo ni plural.
segments: A witness who repeats what a neighbour said is offering hearsay,
and an anonymous source who cannot be named deserves extra caution.
teaching.audioText: A witness who repeats what a neighbour said is offering hearsay, and an anonymous source who cannot be named deserves extra caution.

teaching.en: Whether the new stadium is ugly is a matter of opinion, so no record or measurement could ever verify it.
teaching.es: Que el nuevo estadio sea feo es cuestión de opinión, así que ningún registro ni medición podría verificarlo jamás.
teaching.explanationEs: Un juicio de gusto no se comprueba: es a matter of opinion.
segments: Whether the new stadium is ugly is a matter of
opinion, so no record or measurement could ever verify it.
teaching.audioText: Whether the new stadium is ugly is a matter of opinion, so no record or measurement could ever verify it.

teaching.en: An official statement that publishes its official figures is stronger than a rumour that allegedly comes from someone inside the ministry.
teaching.es: Un comunicado oficial que publica sus cifras oficiales es más sólido que un rumor que supuestamente viene de alguien del ministerio.
teaching.explanationEs: Official statement y official figures permiten que cualquiera compruebe el dato.
segments: An official statement that publishes its official figures is stronger than
a rumour that allegedly comes from someone inside the ministry.
teaching.audioText: An official statement that publishes its official figures is stronger than a rumour that allegedly comes from someone inside the ministry.

teaching.en: A sensational headline tempts readers to accept the story at face value, yet a careful reader will verify the key detail before sharing it.
teaching.es: Un titular sensacionalista tienta a los lectores a aceptar la noticia sin cuestionarla, pero un lector cuidadoso verificará el dato clave antes de compartirla.
teaching.explanationEs: At face value = tal como se presenta, sin comprobarlo.
segments: A sensational headline tempts readers to accept the story at face value,
yet a careful reader will verify the key detail before sharing it.
teaching.audioText: A sensational headline tempts readers to accept the story at face value, yet a careful reader will verify the key detail before sharing it.

prompt.es: ¿Qué parte del texto es un hecho comprobable y no una opinión?

choices.text: That the bridge is the ugliest structure in the whole region.
That most residents privately agree with the local blogger.
That the bridge opened in 1998 and cost 2.3 million pounds.

feedback.es: Solo la fecha y el coste figuran en un comunicado que cualquiera puede consultar; lo demás es un juicio de gusto y una suposición sobre otros.

hint.es: Busca el dato que cualquiera podría comprobar en un documento oficial.

origin.text: The town council's press release states that the bridge opened on 4 May 1998 and cost 2.3 million pounds. A local blogger, however, calls it the ugliest structure in the region and claims that most residents privately agree with him.

prompt.es: Completa: «El vídeo supuestamente muestra al alcalde saliendo antes de la reunión.»

answer.text: allegedly

feedback.es: Allegedly señala que lo que muestra el vídeo aún no está demostrado; la frase siguiente confirma que falta la grabación completa.

hint.es: Adverbio que avisa de que nadie lo ha comprobado todavía.

origin.text: A post is circulating online. The video ___ shows the mayor leaving the meeting early, but nobody has produced the full recording.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Un lector atento verificará el dato de forma independiente antes de compartirlo.»

answer.text: A careful reader will verify the detail independently before sharing it
accepted: A careful reader will verify the detail independently before sharing it
Before sharing it a careful reader will verify the detail independently
A careful reader will independently verify the detail before sharing it
Before sharing it a careful reader will independently verify the detail

feedback.es: El adverbio independently cierra la oración principal y before sharing it introduce el momento de la comprobación.

hint.es: Sujeto + will + verify; el adverbio de modo va después del complemento.

prompt.es: ¿Qué actitud adopta la autora ante la promesa del titular?

choices.text: She doubts it, since the company itself gives no firm numbers.
She accepts it as a forecast, although the company sounds cautious.
She doubts it, since the company has a history of broken promises.
She welcomes it, but wants an official statement to follow soon.

feedback.es: Trata la promesa como «unsupported claim»: la propia empresa solo habla de una reducción posible y no da cifras.

origin.text: The headline promises that the new ferry will cut commuting times in half. Yet the company's own statement speaks only of a possible reduction and offers no official figures, so I would treat the promise as an unsupported claim rather than a forecast.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué la locutora no da la noticia por cierta.

choices.text: The story comes from a colleague who is known to invent news.
The story has passed through several people and lacks official confirmation.
The story has been denied in an official statement from the company.
The story is only her own opinion about the plant's future.

feedback.es: La noticia ha pasado por tres personas y no hay comunicado oficial; la locutora no acusa a nadie de mentir.

origin.audio: My colleague insists that the plant will close in June. When I asked how she knew, she admitted that a driver had mentioned it, and he had heard it from someone in the canteen. That is hearsay, passed along three times. Until the company issues an official statement, I will not take it at face value.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con el tipo de enunciado que representa.

pairs: The town records list 12,400 residents.
The scheme has been a disaster.
An insider allegedly leaked the plan.
A friend of a friend told me.

feedback.es: Cada frase encaja en un tipo distinto: dato de registro, juicio, afirmación sin pruebas y rumor.

pairs: The town records list 12,400 residents.
The scheme has been a disaster.
An insider allegedly leaked the plan.
A friend of a friend told me.

prompt.es: Escucha el pódcast y elige lo que la locutora da a entender sobre la noticia.

choices.text: The plant will almost certainly close, whatever the company says in public.
The website invented its anonymous source to attract more readers.
Repeating an unverified headline can turn a rumour into accepted fact.
Companies should never comment on rumours about their own plans.

feedback.es: La locutora admite que el rumor podría ser cierto, pero critica que se presentara como hecho y se repitiera sin comprobar: así «a worry becomes a fact».

origin.audio: Last week a local website ran a story under the headline Plant to Close, Hundreds to Lose Jobs. Within hours it had been shared thousands of times. I phoned the company, and a spokesperson told me that no decision had been taken and that an official statement would follow on Friday. The website's only source was an anonymous message posted by someone who claimed to work there. Of course, the rumour may turn out to be true. But the writer presented a possibility as a verifiable fact, and readers who took the headline at face value went on to repeat it. That, in my view, is how a worry becomes a fact.

prompt.es: ¿Qué enunciado del informe es una afirmación sin pruebas y no un hecho ni una opinión?

choices.text: That 62 per cent of commuters now take the bus.
That the new timetable is the best thing in years.
That the survey included 400 commuters.
That congestion has fallen by half.

feedback.es: Se dice que el municipio tiene pruebas de la bajada, pero no las ha publicado: es una afirmación sin respaldo. El porcentaje y la muestra son datos; «the best» es opinión.

origin.text: The survey of 400 commuters, published in March, found that 62 per cent now take the bus. The report adds that the new timetable is the best thing to happen to the city in years, and the mayor's office allegedly has proof that congestion has fallen by half, although it has not released it.

prompt.es: Completa: «Es una afirmación sin respaldo, no un hallazgo.»

answer.text: claim

feedback.es: Sin ensayo ni médico citado, el folleto solo ofrece una afirmación sin respaldo: unsupported claim es la colocación habitual.

origin.text: The leaflet insists that its special tea prevents colds in a day. It quotes no trial and names no doctor, so it amounts to an unsupported ___ rather than a finding.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La fuente anónima ofreció rumores en lugar de pruebas sólidas.»

answer.text: The anonymous source offered hearsay rather than hard evidence
accepted: The anonymous source offered hearsay rather than hard evidence
Rather than hard evidence the anonymous source offered hearsay

feedback.es: Rather than contrapone dos cosas: lo que la fuente ofreció (hearsay) y lo que debería haber ofrecido (hard evidence).

prompt.es: ¿Qué pretende la editora con su comentario sobre el tercer párrafo?

choices.text: To persuade him to tone down a conclusion his figures do not fully support.
To warn him that the provisional report may soon be replaced by a final one.
To accuse him of copying the provisional report without checking it.
To tell him that the official statement proves the scheme worked.

feedback.es: Le pide una formulación más cautelosa porque la conclusión es más fuerte que los datos; no le pide borrar nada ni le acusa de copiar.

origin.text: Dear Tom, thank you for the draft. Before it goes online, please look again at the third paragraph. You wrote that the scheme has been a total failure, yet the only figures you quote come from a provisional report, and the official statement is not out. I would prefer a wording such as appears to have fallen short. Regards, Mia.

prompt.es: Escribe una frase que presente la noticia como afirmación sin pruebas.

answer.text: The post claims that the new bus route cuts journey times in half, but it offers no hard evidence and quotes no official figures.
accepted: The post claims that the new bus route cuts journey times in half, but it offers no hard evidence and quotes no official figures.
The post allegedly proves that the new bus route cuts journey times in half, yet it gives no hard evidence and no official figures.
The website claims that the new route cuts the journey time in half, but it provides no hard evidence and quotes no official figures.

feedback.es: Una afirmación sin respaldo se señala con claims that o allegedly y con la ausencia de hard evidence y de cifras oficiales.

origin.text: La publicación dice que la nueva ruta de autobús reduce a la mitad el tiempo de viaje, pero no aporta pruebas sólidas ni cifras oficiales.

prompt.es: Completa: «Demasiados lectores se creen cualquier titular sensacionalista sin más.»

answer.text: take

feedback.es: At face value se combina con take, accept o read: aceptar algo tal como se presenta, sin cuestionarlo.

origin.text: Many readers never ask who wrote a story. Too many of them ___ every sensational headline at face value, and that is how rumours spread.

es: Distinguir causa, correlación y posibilidad con el verbo adecuado (causes, is linked to, may account for) y corregir causas exageradas.

vocabulary.es: causalidad, relación de causa y efecto
no necesariamente, no tiene por qué

teaching.en: A correlation shows that two measurements move together, but causation needs a mechanism that explains why one produces the other.
teaching.es: Una correlación muestra que dos mediciones se mueven juntas, pero la causalidad necesita un mecanismo que explique por qué una produce la otra.
teaching.explanationEs: Correlation y causation son incontables; se contrastan con but.
segments: A correlation shows that two measurements move together, but causation
needs a mechanism that explains why one produces the other.
teaching.audioText: A correlation shows that two measurements move together, but causation needs a mechanism that explains why one produces the other.

teaching.en: Ice cream sales and swimming accidents both show a sharp rise in July, yet the correlation is spurious, since hot weather drives both.
teaching.es: Las ventas de helados y los accidentes al nadar muestran un aumento brusco en julio, pero la correlación es espuria, pues el calor impulsa ambos.
teaching.explanationEs: Spurious: dos datos coinciden sin que uno influya en el otro.
segments: Ice cream sales and swimming accidents both show a sharp rise in
July, yet the correlation is spurious, since hot weather drives both.
teaching.audioText: Ice cream sales and swimming accidents both show a sharp rise in July, yet the correlation is spurious, since hot weather drives both.

teaching.en: Several studies confirm the underlying trend, but it does not necessarily follow that we have found the cause.
teaching.es: Varios estudios confirman la tendencia de fondo, pero no se deduce necesariamente que hayamos encontrado la causa.
teaching.explanationEs: Does not necessarily + verbo base: «no tiene por qué».
segments: Several studies confirm the underlying trend, but it does
not necessarily follow that we have found the cause.
teaching.audioText: Several studies confirm the underlying trend, but it does not necessarily follow that we have found the cause.

teaching.en: Poor sleep is linked to lower exam marks, yet a link of that kind is not the same as a cause.
teaching.es: Dormir mal está relacionado con notas más bajas, pero un vínculo así no es lo mismo que una causa.
teaching.explanationEs: Is linked to describe una relación observada, sin decir qué provoca qué.
segments: Poor sleep is linked to lower exam marks, yet a link
of that kind is not the same as a cause.
teaching.audioText: Poor sleep is linked to lower exam marks, yet a link of that kind is not the same as a cause.

teaching.en: Illness is a contributing factor, not the sole cause: it leads to missed lessons, which may account for part of the fall.
teaching.es: La enfermedad es un factor que contribuye, no la única causa: provoca clases perdidas, que pueden explicar parte de la caída.
teaching.explanationEs: Leads to afirma un efecto; may account for deja una explicación posible.
segments: Illness is a contributing factor, not the sole cause: it leads
to missed lessons, which may account for part of the fall.
teaching.audioText: Illness is a contributing factor, not the sole cause: it leads to missed lessons, which may account for part of the fall.

teaching.en: It may be pure coincidence that two charts move together, so careful writers avoid saying that one causes the other.
teaching.es: Puede ser pura casualidad que dos gráficos se muevan juntos, así que los autores cuidadosos evitan decir que uno causa el otro.
teaching.explanationEs: Coincidence = casualidad; el modal may marca duda.
segments: It may be pure coincidence that two charts move together,
so careful writers avoid saying that one causes the other.
teaching.audioText: It may be pure coincidence that two charts move together, so careful writers avoid saying that one causes the other.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase resume el resultado del estudio sin exagerar?

choices.text: Sleep is linked to better scores, but other factors may matter too.
Sleep causes better exam scores, as the study clearly shows for every group.
Better exam scores lead to longer sleep, according to the researchers involved.

feedback.es: El estudio no controló dieta, estrés ni ingresos, así que solo permite hablar de una relación y de otros factores posibles.

hint.es: Elige la frase que describe una relación y deja abiertos otros factores.

origin.text: Researchers tracked 2,000 students for a year. Those who slept more than eight hours scored higher in every exam, but the study did not control for diet, stress or family income.

prompt.es: Completa: «Quizá el nuevo carril explique parte de la mejora.»

answer.text: account

feedback.es: Account for + sustantivo presenta una explicación posible; el modal may mantiene la cautela y la segunda frase ofrece otra causa.

hint.es: Verbo frasal que significa «explicar» y se construye con for.

origin.text: After the new bus lane opened, journeys became faster. The lane may ___ for part of the improvement, although the repairs ended at the same time.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Las dos tendencias podrían ser una simple casualidad.»

answer.text: The two trends could simply be a coincidence
accepted: The two trends could simply be a coincidence
The two trends could be simply a coincidence

feedback.es: Could + simply + be + a coincidence: el modal de duda y el adverbio suavizan la afirmación.

hint.es: El modal could va antes de simply y del verbo be.

prompt.es: ¿Qué error de razonamiento comete el autor del texto?

choices.text: He compares cities of very different sizes without adjusting the figures.
He treats a correlation between two figures as proof of a cause.
He assumes the trend is a pure coincidence without looking at the figures.
He overlooks that school results have risen sharply in every city.

feedback.es: El autor pasa de «más bibliotecas, mejores resultados» a «las bibliotecas mejoran los resultados» sin mecanismo ni otros factores: confunde una correlación con una causa.

origin.text: Cities with more libraries have better school results. Libraries therefore improve results, and councils should open ten more. Nobody has asked whether richer cities simply have both more libraries and better schools.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué sugiere la economista sobre cafeterías y empresas nuevas.

choices.text: Cafés help start-ups, although the headline overstates the effect.
The link is a coincidence produced by the way cities were chosen.
A third factor, local income, probably explains both.
Start-ups attract cafés, so the direction of cause is reversed.

feedback.es: Para ella, los ingresos locales son el factor que contribuye a ambos hechos; no dice que los cafés ayuden ni que la relación sea casual.

origin.audio: A newspaper reports that cities with more cafés have more start-ups, and concludes that coffee shops help new companies to grow. The expert interviewed is not convinced. She says the link is real, but richer districts attract both cafés and new companies. In her view, local income is a contributing factor that explains both, and the headline ignores it.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada expresión con el nivel de certeza que transmite.

pairs: Heavy rain leads to flooding.
Sleep is linked to better marks.
Illness may account for the fall.
The link is a spurious correlation.

feedback.es: Cada frase comunica un nivel distinto: causa, relación, posibilidad y correlación espuria.

pairs: Heavy rain leads to flooding.
Sleep is linked to better marks.
Illness may account for the fall.
The link is a spurious correlation.

prompt.es: Completa: causa comprobada en la primera frase y factor contribuyente en la segunda.

answer.text: leads | factor

feedback.es: La primera frase afirma una causa probada con leads to; la segunda presenta los ingresos como contributing factor, no como causa única.

sentences: Three large trials show that chronic sleep loss ___ to a drop in attention in class.
Family income is probably a contributing ___ in both trends, so the link is not proven.
origin.text: A health agency reviewed the research on sleep and school results.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige la postura de la presentadora ante la afirmación del municipio.

choices.text: The cameras probably did nothing, since other changes explain the drop.
The council is wrong, because accidents fell on similar roads too.
The drop is certainly a coincidence, so the cameras deserve no credit.
The cameras may have helped, but the evidence does not prove it.

feedback.es: Admite que las cámaras podrían explicar parte de la caída, pero pide una comparación: no la descarta ni la da por probada.

origin.audio: When the city installed speed cameras on Harbour Road, serious accidents fell by a third in two years, and the council was quick to claim the credit. I am not so sure. Over the same period the road was repaired, a new bridge opened, and a petrol price rise kept many drivers at home. Each of these could be a contributing factor. The cameras may well account for part of the drop, and I would not rule that out. But to say they caused it, on these figures alone, is to mistake a sharp fall for proof. What we need is a comparison with a similar road that received no cameras.

prompt.es: Corrige este titular exagerado con una relación y una duda razonable.

answer.text: Late-night phone use may be linked to anxiety in teenagers, although other factors could also account for it.
accepted: Late-night phone use may be linked to anxiety in teenagers, although other factors could also account for it.
Using phones at night might be associated with anxiety in teenagers, but other contributing factors may account for it.
There may be a correlation between late-night phones and anxiety in teenagers, although other factors could account for it.

feedback.es: Un titular exagerado se corrige con is linked to, associated with o correlation, un modal de duda y una mención a otros factores.

origin.text: Titular: «Los celulares de noche causan ansiedad en los adolescentes.» Reescríbelo con una relación y un modal de duda, y menciona que otros factores podrían explicarlo.

prompt.es: Ordena: «El fuerte aumento de precios puede explicar ambas tendencias.»

answer.text: The strong rise in prices may account for both trends

feedback.es: May account for presenta el aumento de precios como explicación posible de las dos tendencias.

prompt.es: ¿Con qué propósito aparece la última frase del texto?

choices.text: To warn that the link may work in the opposite direction.
To show that feeling lonely makes adults less able to care for a dog.
To argue that adopting a dog is still the best answer to loneliness.
To suggest that the figures are a coincidence without any meaning.

feedback.es: La frase final propone que la causalidad podría ir al revés: quienes ya se sienten bien adoptan más perros.

origin.text: The figures are striking: in towns where more people own a dog, fewer adults report feeling lonely. Nobody should conclude, however, that adopting a dog is an answer to loneliness. People who already feel well may simply be readier to take one on, and the direction of cause may run the other way.

prompt.es: Completa: «La correlación es espuria: los mayores calzan más y leen mejor.»

answer.text: spurious

feedback.es: Una correlación spurious aparece cuando un tercer factor (la edad) explica ambos datos y no hay conexión real entre ellos.

origin.text: Shoe size and reading ability are strongly linked in primary schools. The correlation is ___, because older children simply have bigger feet and also read better.

prompt.es: Ordena: «La correlación espuria desapareció al incluir el calor.»

answer.text: The spurious correlation disappeared once the heat was included
accepted: The spurious correlation disappeared once the heat was included
Once the heat was included the spurious correlation disappeared

feedback.es: Once introduce la condición que hizo desaparecer la correlación: al incluir el calor, el vínculo dejó de existir.

es: Reconocer en publicaciones breves el falso dilema, la generalización apresurada, el ataque personal y el sesgo, y nombrar la debilidad con una razón.

teaching.en: Flawed reasoning often hides in a fallacy, a step that sounds convincing but collapses the moment someone examines it closely.
teaching.es: El razonamiento defectuoso suele esconderse en una falacia, un paso que suena convincente pero se derrumba en cuanto alguien lo examina de cerca.
teaching.explanationEs: Fallacy se refiere a un fallo del argumento, no a un dato falso.
segments: Flawed reasoning often hides in a fallacy, a step that
sounds convincing but collapses the moment someone examines it closely.
teaching.audioText: Flawed reasoning often hides in a fallacy, a step that sounds convincing but collapses the moment someone examines it closely.

teaching.en: Either we ban phones completely or students will never concentrate: a false dilemma hides a weakness, because other options exist.
teaching.es: O prohibimos los celulares por completo o los alumnos nunca se concentrarán: un falso dilema esconde un punto débil, porque existen otras opciones.
teaching.explanationEs: Un falso dilema reduce la realidad a dos opciones.
segments: Either we ban phones completely or students will never concentrate:
a false dilemma hides a weakness, because other options exist.
teaching.audioText: Either we ban phones completely or students will never concentrate: a false dilemma hides a weakness, because other options exist.

teaching.en: Two rude tourists are an unrepresentative sample, so it would be a hasty generalisation to assume that every visitor behaves the same way.
teaching.es: Dos turistas groseros son una muestra no representativa, así que sería una generalización apresurada suponer que todos los visitantes se comportan igual.
teaching.explanationEs: Assume que + oración: no lleva preposición.
segments: Two rude tourists are an unrepresentative sample, so it would be a
hasty generalisation to assume that every visitor behaves the same way.
teaching.audioText: Two rude tourists are an unrepresentative sample, so it would be a hasty generalisation to assume that every visitor behaves the same way.

teaching.en: When a reply criticises the speaker's age instead of her argument, it is a personal attack, and the original weakness remains untouched.
teaching.es: Cuando una réplica critica la edad de la oradora en lugar de su argumento, es un ataque personal, y el punto débil original queda sin tocar.
teaching.explanationEs: El ataque personal desvía la atención del argumento hacia quien habla.
segments: When a reply criticises the speaker's age instead of her argument,
it is a personal attack, and the original weakness remains untouched.
teaching.audioText: When a reply criticises the speaker's age instead of her argument, it is a personal attack, and the original weakness remains untouched.

teaching.en: To build a straw man, a writer distorts an opponent's view and then defeats the distortion, a fallacy that rewards careless listeners.
teaching.es: Para construir un hombre de paja, un autor distorsiona la postura de un rival y luego derrota esa distorsión, una falacia que premia a los oyentes descuidados.
teaching.explanationEs: Straw man = versión deformada de lo que dijo el otro.
segments: To build a straw man, a writer distorts an opponent's view
and then defeats the distortion, a fallacy that rewards careless listeners.
teaching.audioText: To build a straw man, a writer distorts an opponent's view and then defeats the distortion, a fallacy that rewards careless listeners.

teaching.en: Survey bias appears when a writer decides to cherry-pick only the answers that support the conclusion, which produces a one-sided picture.
teaching.es: El sesgo de una encuesta aparece cuando un autor decide elegir solo las respuestas que apoyan la conclusión, lo que da una imagen parcial.
teaching.explanationEs: Bias es incontable en este sentido; one-sided se escribe con guion.
segments: Survey bias appears when a writer decides to cherry-pick only the
answers that support the conclusion, which produces a one-sided picture.
teaching.audioText: Survey bias appears when a writer decides to cherry-pick only the answers that support the conclusion, which produces a one-sided picture.

prompt.es: ¿Qué debilidad tiene esta publicación?

choices.text: It is a hasty generalisation: it builds a rule from very few cases.
It is a false dilemma: it offers two options when others exist.
It is a personal attack: it criticises people instead of ideas.

feedback.es: La publicación presenta dos caminos como únicos; «there is simply no other choice» es la señal de un falso dilema.

hint.es: Fíjate en la estructura either … or y en la frase que niega cualquier otra opción.

origin.text: Either we ban every phone in school or our results will keep falling. There is simply no other choice, and pretending otherwise only wastes everyone's time.

prompt.es: Completa: «Decir que todos los turistas son groseros es una generalización apresurada.»

answer.text: generalisation

feedback.es: Hasty generalisation es el nombre de la falacia que convierte dos casos en una regla general.

hint.es: Sustantivo: regla general sacada de pocos casos.

origin.text: Two rude tourists tell us very little about millions of visitors. To conclude that every tourist is rude is a hasty ___ drawn from an unrepresentative sample.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Su réplica fue un ataque personal que ignoró por completo mi argumento.»

answer.text: Her reply was a personal attack that ignored my argument completely

feedback.es: Personal attack + that ignored…: la relativa explica por qué el ataque no resuelve nada: el argumento ni se examina.

hint.es: Empieza por el sujeto Her reply; completely va al final.

prompt.es: ¿Qué debilidad tiene la encuesta del texto?

choices.text: The survey is too old to describe what the town thinks today.
The percentage is misleading, because the pool's cost is never mentioned.
Only people already using the pool were asked, so the sample cannot speak for the town.
The question was worded so that members could only answer yes.

feedback.es: Solo se preguntó a quienes salían de la piscina un sábado: una muestra no representativa que no puede hablar en nombre de toda la ciudad.

origin.text: Our club's survey shows that 95 per cent of members love the new pool. We asked only the people leaving the pool on Saturday morning, but the result is clear: the whole town is delighted.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué hizo Sara en el debate.

choices.text: She exposed the lack of evidence behind his proposal.
She distorted his proposal and then defeated the distorted version.
She offered two extreme options and ignored every other one.
She attacked his background instead of examining his proposal.

feedback.es: Sara desvió la atención hacia la persona de Carlos; por eso su punto débil real, la falta de pruebas, no llegó a discutirse.

origin.audio: Carlos argued for longer school days. His opponent, Sara, did not answer him. Instead she said that a man who never teaches could hardly understand pupils. Everyone cheered, but notice what happened: she attacked the speaker, not the argument. His proposal was never discussed, and its real weakness, a lack of evidence, was never exposed.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada enunciado con la debilidad que muestra.

pairs: Either we ban phones or students fail.
Two rude drivers, so everyone here drives badly.
You are too young to judge this.
She quoted only the figures that helped her.

feedback.es: Cada enunciado ejemplifica una debilidad distinta: dos opciones, pocos casos, ataque a la persona y datos escogidos.

pairs: Either we ban phones or students fail.
Two rude drivers, so everyone here drives badly.
You are too young to judge this.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige lo que la locutora da a entender sobre el proyecto del estacionamiento.

choices.text: It may be a good idea, even though its defence is weak.
It is a bad idea, because the mayor defends it so badly.
The survey proves that the car park will not help any shop.
The shop owner's interest means that her survey is useless.

feedback.es: La locutora admite que el estacionamiento «may well help», pero critica el argumento que lo defiende: no descalifica el proyecto, solo su defensa.

origin.audio: A local mayor posted a message online. Either the town builds a new car park, he wrote, or shops will close one by one. When a shop owner replied that an earlier survey had suggested other options, the mayor answered that she was hardly a neutral voice, since her own shop was beside the market. Notice what is missing: he never discussed her survey, and he offered no figures of his own. His case rests on two weak steps: a choice between only two futures, and the rejection of the person who questions it. The car park may well help. But the argument in its favour is a poor one.

prompt.es: ¿Qué debilidad tiene la respuesta del bloguero?

choices.text: It assumes that every student dislikes homework on any topic.
It distorts her proposal and then attacks the distorted version.
It draws a general rule from two or three students' behaviour.
It criticises the teacher's character instead of her suggestion.

feedback.es: El bloguero convierte «un poco de elección» en «hacer lo que quieran» y rebate esa versión deformada: es un hombre de paja, no un ataque personal.

origin.text: Teacher: We should give students a little choice about their homework topics. Blogger: So the teacher wants students to do whatever they like and never work hard. Schools cannot run on doing nothing, and a school that trusts its pupils to choose will soon lose control, so her idea must be rejected.

prompt.es: Completa: «El autor está eligiendo solo las pruebas que encajan con su tesis.»

feedback.es: Cherry-picking describe elegir solo los datos favorables y dejar fuera el resto: el informe cita tres estudios a favor e ignora los otros diez.

origin.text: The report mentions the three studies that support the plan and ignores the other ten. The writer is clearly cherry-___ the evidence to suit his case.

prompt.es: Nombra la debilidad de esta publicación y da una razón con because.

answer.text: This is a hasty generalisation, because it draws a general rule about every app from the experience of one person.
accepted: This is a hasty generalisation, because it draws a general rule about every app from the experience of one person.
It is a hasty generalisation, since it builds a general rule about all apps from just one person's experience.
The post is a hasty generalization because one case cannot prove anything about every app.

feedback.es: Se nombra la falacia (hasty generalisation) y se justifica con because: un solo caso no permite hablar de todas las apps.

origin.text: Publicación: «Mi primo probó esa app y no le funcionó, así que ninguna app sirve para aprender idiomas.» Nombra la debilidad y explica por qué.

prompt.es: ¿Qué opina el autor del aplauso del público?

choices.text: It proves the minister answered his critics in a convincing way.
It was unfair, because the audience had not seen the figures.
It shows enthusiasm more than it proves that the argument was sound.
It was deserved, even though the minister skipped the figures.

feedback.es: El autor dice que el aplauso revela más entusiasmo que calidad del argumento: el ministro ni siquiera mencionó las cifras de sus rivales.

origin.text: In his closing speech the minister claimed that critics of the plan were friends of chaos. He did not mention the figures his opponents had produced. The audience cheered loudly, which says more about its enthusiasm than about the quality of the argument, and the newspapers then repeated the slogan without checking it.

answer.text: unrepresentative

feedback.es: Una muestra elegida en una sola calle es unrepresentative: no refleja la variedad de la ciudad.

origin.text: A survey of twenty people, all chosen from one street, cannot speak for the whole town. The sample is ___.

es: Escribir una crítica matizada de una publicación: dos críticas justificadas, una relación con modal de duda y una alternativa razonable.

sample, which is arguably its most serious weakness.
teaching.audioText: The post seems to overlook the size of the sample, which is arguably its most serious weakness.

teaching.en: The link between the two charts is tenuous, so the evidence may fall short of what such a bold claim requires.

prompt.es: ¿Qué versión formula mejor una crítica con matices?

choices.text: The post is nonsense, because nobody should trust any writer who loves bans so much.
The post is completely right, although it might still need one more good example.
The post seems to overlook other changes, so the ban may explain only part of it.

feedback.es: La primera crítica es cauta y razonada: señala un punto que se pasa por alto y deja abierta la explicación.

hint.es: Busca la crítica que da una razón concreta y usa un verbo de cautela.

origin.text: Since the school banned sweets, pupils have become calmer. The ban obviously works, and every school should copy it at once.

answer.text: fall

origin.text: The writer surveyed only two classes out of twenty. Her findings ___ short of what a general claim requires.

prompt.es: Ordena: «En lugar de culpar a los alumnos, pregunta por qué están cansados.»

answer.text: Rather than blaming students ask why they are tired
accepted: Rather than blaming students ask why they are tired
Ask why they are tired rather than blaming students

feedback.es: Rather than + gerundio contrapone una acción rechazada (culpar) con la preferida (preguntar).

hint.es: Empieza con Rather than y un gerundio; después va la orden.

prompt.es: ¿Qué sostiene la crítica sobre la relación entre ir en bici y las notas?

choices.text: That it is real but small, because only two classes were compared.
That it is pure coincidence, since only two classes were surveyed.
That it is reversed, because good marks make pupils want to cycle.

feedback.es: La crítica llama «tenuous» a la relación porque alumnos con más recursos o mejor forma física podrían explicar ambos datos.

origin.text: The post claims that cycling to school improves marks. Arguably, its main weakness is the sample: only two classes, both in richer districts. The link between cycling and marks is tenuous, since fitter or better-off pupils may cycle more and also study better. A reasonable alternative would be to compare pupils from different districts.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige la actitud de la locutora hacia la publicación de su amiga.

choices.text: Friendly but firm: she questions the method and proposes a fairer test.
Friendly but evasive: she hides her doubts and lets the post stand.
Critical only: she lists the flaws and suggests no better test.
Sceptical of the app: she doubts that any app can be tested fairly.

feedback.es: Sus dudas son concretas (tres días, sin comparación) y propone una alternativa: una crítica amable pero firme.

origin.audio: My friend's post about a new app was kind, but I had two concerns. First, she had used it for only three days, so her praise may fall short of a fair test. Second, she compared it with nothing. I suggested that she try another app for a week and report both results. She laughed, then agreed that her post was open to question.

A reasonable alternative would be to ask every class.
The rise is likely to be linked to the rules.

feedback.es: Cada frase cumple un papel distinto: crítica cautelosa, concesión, propuesta y relación probable.

prompt.es: ¿Qué crítica de la publicación resulta más sólida y equilibrada?

choices.text: It proves that silence works, although a few pupils disliked it at first.
Its evidence is a few interviews and anecdotes, so a national rule is open to question.
It relies on teachers' opinions alone, so the pupils' view is missing entirely.
It should have interviewed every single pupil, because three opinions can never mean anything.

feedback.es: La crítica válida señala el punto débil (pocas entrevistas y unas anécdotas) y duda de la generalización, sin rechazar toda la publicación.

origin.text: Last term our school introduced a silent lunch hour, and the results are surprising. Complaints about noise fell by half, and teachers say that afternoon lessons are calmer. One teacher told me that pupils now return to class ready to work. Some students complained at first, but they soon adapted. I interviewed three of them, and all three admitted that they prefer the quiet. A parent also told me that her son comes home less tired and does his homework without any argument. So the policy is a success, and every school in the country should adopt it immediately, because silence is exactly what teenagers need.

origin.text: The numbers in the report are accurate. However, the survey method may ___ doubts about the conclusion, because nobody checked how the pupils were chosen.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige lo que la locutora deja entrever con el final de la historia.

choices.text: That the author was offended and chose to end the discussion.
That the critic had been rude in his last message to her.
That the author may have had no good answer to that point.
That the survey was repeated and confirmed the pattern.

feedback.es: El silencio final sugiere que la autora no tenía buena respuesta a la última objeción; el texto no dice que se ofendiera ni que repitiera la encuesta.

origin.audio: The author of the post replied politely. She accepted that her sample was small, but insisted that the pattern was clear. The critic answered that a clear pattern in a small sample is exactly what chance produces, and asked whether she would repeat the survey with more classes. The author did not reply again.

prompt.es: Escribe una crítica matizada de la publicación (220–280 palabras).

answer.text: The post makes an interesting point, but I think its conclusion needs more care. First, the writer seems to overlook the size of the sample: only thirty pupils from one class were asked, so the result may fall short of what a general claim requires. Second, the post rests on the idea that headphones stop fights, but it gives no evidence of how the fights were counted, which leaves the method open to question. To some extent, the fall in fights is likely to be linked to the headphones, although other factors, such as the weather or a new teacher, may also account for it. Arguably, the pupils who use headphones are simply the quiet ones, so the link is tenuous. Rather than handing out headphones in every school, a reasonable alternative would be to survey several classes for a whole term and compare the results. A balanced critique must also admit that the idea is worth testing, and I would certainly support a careful trial.
accepted: The post makes an interesting point, but I think its conclusion needs more care. First, the writer seems to overlook the size of the sample: only thirty pupils from one class were asked, so the result may fall short of what a general claim requires. Second, the post rests on the idea that headphones stop fights, but it gives no evidence of how the fights were counted, which leaves the method open to question. To some extent, the fall in fights is likely to be linked to the headphones, although other factors, such as the weather or a new teacher, may also account for it. Arguably, the pupils who use headphones are simply the quiet ones, so the link is tenuous. Rather than handing out headphones in every school, a reasonable alternative would be to survey several classes for a whole term and compare the results. A balanced critique must also admit that the idea is worth testing, and I would certainly support a careful trial.

I found the post interesting, but its argument needs more care. To begin with, the writer seems to overlook how small the sample was: thirty pupils from a single class cannot speak for a whole school, so the evidence falls short of a general rule. Besides, the post never explains how the fights were counted, and that raises doubts about the method. To some extent, the calmer breaks are likely to be linked to the headphones, but a new teacher, better weather or a different timetable could also account for them. Arguably, the link is tenuous, because quiet pupils may be the ones who choose headphones. Rather than giving headphones to every school, a reasonable alternative would be to compare several classes over a full term. A balanced critique should add that the idea deserves a serious trial, and I would gladly help to organise one, even if the final results turned out to be smaller than the post promises.

feedback.es: Una crítica matizada nombra dos debilidades con su razón, relaciona dos datos con duda, concede un punto y propone una alternativa.

prompt.es: ¿Con qué intención escribe Luna su correo?

To praise the argument while asking Mar to correct a few small mistakes in her figures.
To reject the post as unreliable and ask Mar to delete it.
To voice constructive doubts and suggest a fairer comparison.

feedback.es: Luna elogia el argumento, señala dos puntos discutibles y propone comparar con otro colegio: una crítica constructiva.

origin.text: Dear Mar, thank you for sharing your post about the new timetable. I enjoyed the argument, but two points seem open to question. You say that lessons are shorter because pupils are happier, yet the change may simply be due to the new bell. Could you check the numbers again? A comparison with another school would be a reasonable alternative. Best wishes, Luna.

That the ban had no effect on pupils under twelve.
That the rise in results may have another explanation.

origin.audio: The story spread quickly: a school in the north had supposedly banned homework, saved millions and raised exam results. We checked three claims. First, the ban: the head teacher confirmed it, but only for pupils under twelve, so the claim is partly true. Second, the saving: no figure has been published, so we rate it as unproven. Third, the rise in results: it is real, yet the school changed its exam board in the same year, which makes the claim misleading. Our tentative conclusion is that the homework ban may have helped, but the evidence does not yet show it.

prompt.es: ¿Qué evidencia falta para sostener que el tranvía salva vidas?

A quote from a doctor saying that the tram is good for the town.
